timings_excluded: ONE run of ONE corpus (base_10, 26 source rows) at ONE class (M). The per-stage seconds below are dominated by fixed overhead at this size and must not be read as throughput. They are recorded for the ORCHESTRATION question — how much wall-clock the pod boundaries cost, and whether a chain pays a cold node per link — not as a performance claim.
what_this_answers: batch-orchestration-design §11 Phase 3's dev-cluster acceptance (a pipeline run as per-attempt Kubernetes Jobs on the real cluster) and the first real input to Phase 5.

orchestration_cost.note: Six gaps for seven stages. Each gap covers settle -> readiness evaluation -> Job create -> schedule -> container start on an already-warm node. At this corpus size the overhead is 63% of wall clock; it is a FIXED cost per stage, so its share falls as the corpus grows. Sizing a real comparison against the monolith needs a corpus where the bodies dominate - that run has not been done.

findings.finding: A chain does NOT pay a cold node per link.
findings.detail: All seven stages ran on one node (i-090cab885a077db38). The runner NodePools are consolidationPolicy WhenEmpty / consolidateAfter 30s, and the measured inter-stage gaps are 3-5s - comfortably inside that window - so the node survives between stages. docs/research-runner-startup.md §1 worried that 'every link pays the full cold start, because the previous node was already reclaimed 30 s after its pod exited'. For a stage chain at this cadence it does not.
findings.caveat: This is a property of the GAP, not of the design. A stage whose predecessor takes longer than consolidateAfter to hand over, or a job that waits on the in-flight cap, would provision afresh.

findings.finding: Consolidation does reclaim the node promptly once the chain ends.
findings.detail: The node was NotFound within minutes of the final stage finishing, and the runner node count returned to 2. So the 30s reclaim is working; it simply never fires mid-chain.
